sections.skill: Use the equation of a linear model to interpret the slope and intercept and to make predictions

questions.skill: Use the equation of a linear model to interpret the slope and intercept and to make predictions
questions.prompt: A line of fit for the height h (inches) of a plant after w weeks is h = 1.5w + 4. What do the slope and the intercept mean?
questions.prompt_markup:
A line of fit for the height h (inches) of a plant after w weeks is h = 1.5w + 4.
What do the slope and the intercept mean?
questions.correct_answer: Slope: the plant grows about 1.5 inches per week. Intercept: it was about 4 inches tall at week 0.

questions.skill: Use the equation of a linear model to interpret the slope and intercept and to make predictions

questions.prompt_markup:

choices.text: The level rises about 0.3 foot each day.

The level drops about 0.3 foot each day.

questions.skill: Interpret the slope and intercept of a linear model in context
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A model for the number n of ice pops sold on a day with a high temperature of t °F is n = 4t - 200. What does the slope mean?
questions.prompt_markup:
A model for the number n of ice pops sold on a day with a high temperature of t °F is n = 4t - 200.
What does the slope mean?
questions.correct_answer: About 4 more ice pops are sold for each 1 °F rise in temperature.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data

questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A model for ice-pop sales is n = 4t - 200, where t is the temperature in °F. Does the intercept -200 make sense in this situation? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
A model for ice-pop sales is n = 4t - 200, where t is the temperature in °F.
Does the intercept -200 make sense in this situation? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: No. It would mean -200 ice pops sold at 0 °F, but sales cannot be negative.

sections.skill: Evaluate reports and predictions based on data

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Evaluate reports and predictions based on data
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A model of children's heights for ages 2 to 10 is h = 2.5a + 31 inches at age a. A report uses it to predict the height of a 40-year-old. Is that reasonable? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
A model of children's heights for ages 2 to 10 is h = 2.5a + 31 inches at age a.
A report uses it to predict the height of a 40-year-old. Is that reasonable? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: No. It predicts 131 inches (about 11 feet). The model fits only ages 2 to 10, so using it far outside the data is not reliable.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions

questions.prompt: A line of fit was made from data collected between 60 °F and 90 °F. A report uses it to predict sales at 70 °F. Is that reasonable? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
A line of fit was made from data collected between 60 °F and 90 °F.
A report uses it to predict sales at 70 °F. Is that reasonable? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. 70 °F is inside the range of the data.
